{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Contract review against playbook — findings and proposed positions
**Client posture:** We represent Corio (Customer/Licensee).

---

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Agreement. The commercial architecture is, on the whole, favourable to us: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no non-solicitation, no MFN, no minimum purchase or volume commitment and no liquidated damages or penalty payable by us. The vendor indemnity in Section 8 is strong and, because Section 9 carves Section 8 liability out of both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, it is effectively uncapped in our favour. Renewal terms (12-month auto-renewal, 30-day opt-out, fixed pricing for Years 2–5 and beyond) sit at our preferred position.

Eight items require attention. The one item of real substance is **termination for convenience**: the Agreement runs a five-year initial term with exit only for uncured material breach or insolvency, leaving us with no convenience right. That finding is flagged for internal verification before it is raised with the counterparty. Beyond that, the principal gaps are **IP ownership** (Developments supported by Commerce One flip to Commerce One with no licence back, and no protection for Corio/Customer data), **post-termination transition and data return** (absent entirely), **limitation of liability** (the cap is restricted to fees for the related transaction and lacks confidentiality/gross negligence/wilful misconduct carve-outs), **warranty duration** (60 days with a hard December 31, 1999 outside date), **governing law forum** (mandatory AAA arbitration rather than California courts), **licence scope** (no affiliate coverage), **assignment** (consent may be withheld arbitrarily) and **audit** and **insurance** clean-ups.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 Indemnification | At or above fallback: full IP infringement defence for Corio and its Customers, complete remedy ladder, narrow exclusions, and uncapped by virtue of the Section 9 carve-out. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Shared Resources | Section 13.5 flips ownership of Developments to Commerce One where it provides ongoing support, with no licence back; no clause addresses Corio/Customer data. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 11 Term and Termination | Five-year initial term; § 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. No Corio convenience right. To be re-verified internally before raising. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14 Miscellaneous | No exclusivity binds us; Section 2 grants are non-exclusive, § 14.8 preserves our right to subcontract, Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No liquidated damages, penalty, late charge, minimum-on-termination or early-termination fee payable by Corio. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 13 Shared Resources | No non-compete binds us; § 13.6 expressly preserves independent development. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 14 Miscellaneous | California law is at our accepted fallback, but mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration in San Francisco fails the fallback forum element. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 3 (2. Grant of Rights) | Grants run to Corio only; "affiliate" appears nowhere and there is no mechanism to add affiliates. Transferability via § 14.1 is satisfied. |
| Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14 Miscellaneous | Mutual clause with an M&A successor carve-out, but consent may be withheld arbitrarily and the successor route has no written notice mechanic. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 (7. Warranties and Disclaimer) | Remedies meet the fallback, but the 60-day Warranty Period with a December 31, 1999 outside date falls below the 90-day floor. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 11 Term and Termination | No transition assistance, data return, export or deletion obligation anywhere; only mutual return of Confidential Information. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No parity, best-terms, right-to-match or disclosure mechanic in either direction. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4 Fees | Fees payable only for what we license or order; no take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or usage cap. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14 Miscellaneous | No hiring or solicitation covenant anywhere; personnel provisions are operational only. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 11 Term and Termination | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, fees fixed for "Year 2-5, and beyond". Absence of a vendor reminder is noted only. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9 Limitation of Liability | Mutual and carves out Section 8, but the cap is limited to fees "for the transaction which the liability relates to" and lacks confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 4 Fees | Once-yearly, independent CPA acceptable to us, Commerce One-funded — but notice is merely "reasonable" and cost-shifting triggers at 5% rather than 10%. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 Miscellaneous | No insurance covenant; "insurance" appears only as a pricing deduction in the net revenue definition. |

---

## Walk-away items

- **Absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right in a five-year committed term (§ 11.1–11.2).** Our playbook treats no convenience right in a multi-year committed term as walk-away territory; the clause fails even the fallback, which would require a 60–90 day Corio exit. Our position is a new Section 11.2A giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, drafted to name Corio directly so as not to disturb the § 1.6 "CUSTOMER(S)" definition. **Note:** this finding did not pass internal verification and must be re-confirmed against the executed text before it is put to Commerce One.

No other finding reaches walk-away level. In particular, the assignment clause, while a deviation, is not walk-away territory: it is mutual, carries an M&A/substantially-all-assets successor carve-out, and no provision gives Commerce One a termination or re-pricing right on our change of control.

---

## Next steps

1. **Re-verify the T4C finding** against the operative text of §§ 11.1–11.3 and Exhibit B before it is tabled. Once confirmed, lead with it as our priority ask.
2. **Table the two critical/structural redlines:**
   - *IP (§ 13.5):* add a licence back to Corio for Commerce One-owned Developments and limit any Commerce One licence in Corio/Customer data.
   - *Transition (new § 11.4):* assistance for up to six months at then-current rates, return of our and our Customers' data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter.
3. **Table the fallback-conforming edits**, each drafted as the shortest possible change:
   - *§ 9:* delete the per-transaction restriction on the cap and add confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct to the existing exception opener (the Section 8 carve-out is retained).
   - *§ 7.3:* extend the Warranty Period to 90 days and delete the December 31, 1999 outside date; existing remedies and the § 11.2 cross-reference remain intact.
   - *§ 14.3 / § 12.2:* keep California law, substitute exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, and conform the heading and the § 12.2 escrow cross-reference so no dangling arbitration reference remains.
   - *§ 2:* extend the Section 2 licences to Corio affiliates on written notice.
   - *§ 14.1:* add a "not unreasonably withheld" standard to the consent requirement and a written notice mechanic for successor assignments.
   - *§ 4.4:* set a 15-day notice period and raise the audit cost-shifting threshold to a 10% underpayment.
   - *§ 14 (Miscellaneous):* insert a short vendor insurance covenant (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000).
4. **Hold in reserve as upside, not opening asks:** extending the § 8 indemnity to breach of applicable law, Commerce One-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct and to our affiliates; the preferred asymmetric assignment position; the 12-month software warranty and express services/compliance warranties; the USD 1,000,000 liability floor and additional § 9 carve-outs; the preferred audit mechanics (business hours, confidentiality-bound auditor, off-site where possible); and a 60-day vendor renewal reminder.
5. **Commercial observation (no redline):** the Agreement contains no MFN in our favour. Flagging for the business team only."}
